fn.en: Say where you live and where things are.
fn.ru: Говорить, где ты живёшь и где что находится.
fn.kk: Қайда тұратыныңды және не қайда тұрғанын айту.

can.en: I can describe my home and say what is in it.
can.ru: Я могу описать свой дом и сказать, что в нём есть.
can.kk: Үйімді сипаттап, онда не бар екенін айта аламын.

tip.en: There’s + one thing. There are + two or more.
tip.ru: There’s + один предмет. There are + два и больше.
tip.kk: There’s + бір зат. There are + екі және одан көп.

items.q: ___ a small garden behind the house.

items.why: next to + place. “near” works alone: near the lift.

items.q: I live ___ a flat ___ the fourth floor.

items.s: I don’t have a house. I have a ___. 🏢
My flat is on the ninth ___. 🔢
My grandparents live in a small ___. 🏞
We eat and cook in the ___. 🍳

lines: I live [in|on|at] a flat [in|on|at] the ninth floor.
[There’s|There are|It’s] a big kitchen and [there are|there’s|there is a] two bedrooms.
[There isn’t|There aren’t|There not] a garden, but [there’s|there are|it’s] a small balcony.
The bathroom is [next to|next|near to] the kitchen. The toilet is [upstairs|in upstairs|on upstairs].
“Where’s the exit?” — “It’s [over there|there over|over here there], [on the left|in the left|at the left].”

items.a: The kitchen is next to the bathroom

tts: Is there a hotel car park? Yes, there is.
Where are the toilets? They are next to the gym.
Is there a bath in the bathroom? No, there isn’t. But there’s a shower.
Are there any refreshments in the room? Yes, there are. The mini-bar has got tea, coffee and water.

items.s: 2 — the toilets are next to the gym.
3 — there is a bath in the bathroom.
4 — there is tea and coffee in the room.

acts.title: My place
text: I live in a flat in Almaty. 🏙
It’s on the ninth floor, so there’s a lift. 🛗
There are two bedrooms and one bathroom.
There isn’t a garden, but there’s a big kitchen. 🍳
There is a shop next to my house. 🛣

items.s: The writer lives in a house.
The flat is on the ninth floor.
There is a shop next to the house.

items.sit: A new colleague asks where you live. You live in Almaty, in a flat.
o: I live in a flat in Almaty.
I live on a flat in Almaty.
I am live in flat Almaty.

items.sit: You are in a hotel and you need the toilet.
Someone asks: “Is there a lift?” There is one.
Someone asks about your garden. Your flat has none.
A visitor asks where the exit is. It is at the other end of the room.
o: It’s over there, on the right.
It’s there over, in the right.

items.sit: Someone asks how many bedrooms you have. You have two.

lines.s: In a flat in Almaty. ___ a lift, so it’s easy. 🛗
No, there isn’t. And there ___ any trees on my street.
And the toilets in your office — where are they?
Upstairs. Take the lift and they’re over ___. 👉

write.q: Write 5 sentences about your home. Say where you live, what there is and what there isn’t.
write.model: I live in a flat in Almaty. It’s on the fifth floor and there’s a lift. There are two bedrooms and one bathroom. There isn’t a garden, but there’s a big kitchen. The shop is next to my house.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Where do you live? Is there a lift? Then say where the kitchen and the bathroom are.
speak.model: I live in a flat in Almaty. Yes, there is — it’s on the ninth floor. The kitchen is next to the living room and the bathroom is upstairs.
